A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that fine-needle aspiration cytology is an excellent technique for the study of renal mononuclear cell infiltrates, and that the differential counts of mononucleated cells obtained by this technique can be correlated with the clinical manifestations of the patients.
FNAB of renal tissue is a useful tool to detect mononuclear interstial cellular infiltration, and to quantitate the number of infiltrating cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of mononuclear intercellular infiltration, as detected by FNAB, is associated with renal dysfunction, and may be used as an early indicator of the severity of nephritis.
